status_effects.explanation: Froberville's remark nominally elevates her desirability by seeking her out and preferring her to a horrific fate, though the backhanded, comic phrasing keeps the effect weak and ambiguous.

appraisal_events.evidence: le général de Froberville lui demanda à connaître Mme de Cambremer... « Dites donc, Swann, j'aimerais mieux être le mari de cette femme-là que d'être massacré par les sauvages, qu'en dites-vous ? »
appraisal_events.explanation: Froberville seeks an introduction to Mme de Cambremer and pays her a crude, hyperbolic compliment, favoring marriage to her over being killed by 'savages'; the grotesque comparison makes the remark simultaneously flattering and faintly demeaning, with no narratorial gloss to settle which reading dominates.

ambiguities: Froberville's remark about Mme de Cambremer ('j'aimerais mieux être le mari de cette femme-là que d'être massacré par les sauvages') is stylistically comic and could be read either as a genuine, if crude, compliment or as an implicit disparagement given the grotesque comparison; the passage offers no narratorial commentary to resolve this.
